newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslems step up presence in contested village.
newsitem.headline: Moslems step up presence in contested village.

text.p: Bosnian Moslems have increased their presence in a war-devastated village in Serb-controlled territory to about 300 and are hauling in supplies to rebuild houses there, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.
"The number of Moslems has increased to about 300 and we have observed them bringing in building supplies," U.N. spokesman Alex Ivanko said of the situation in Jusici, east of Tuzla.
"Republika Srpska (Bosnian Serb) police are present but they are behaving in a very professional and restrained manner."

About 100 Moslems, some of them armed, entered the village last Friday. Mostly destroyed in the 43-month Bosnian war, Jusici sits inside Serb-held territory and within a demilitarised "zone of separation" patrolled by NATO forces.

NATO troops seized arms from the Moslems and urged Serb authorities not to enter the village, which is their right under the Dayton peace agreement. International officials have sought since Friday to defuse the situation, but with no apparent progress.
"I can tell you that nobody has a solution to this problem," a well-placed international official told Reuters on Wednesday, commenting on nearly a week of fruitless discussion.
Serb authorities insist that the Moslems withdraw and register to re-enter the village according to U.N. guidelines agreed among the parties and the international community in July.
The Moslems, acting on the assumption that in Bosnia possession is everything, are reluctant to pull back now that they have established a presence.
Ivanko said 10 young Moslem men had taunted Serb police in the Jusici area, prompting U.N. police to intervene to prevent the situation getting out of hand.
"One of the Moslems who returned, the former Mayor, helped us get the young men out of the village and the Serbs performed with admirable restraint under the circumstances," the U.N. spokesman said.
